title: Shared servers: efficient until they aren't

source.name: Netflix TechBlog
source.title: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform

description: Netflix wrote about adding VM-level isolation for single-tenant workloads on its Titus container platform.

scenes.narration: Containers share a host. Great for cost. Less great when a neighbour gets loud.
scenes.headline: Shared hosts, shared problems

scenes.narration: Netflix's engineering blog describes single tenant Titus, adding virtual machine level isolation to its multi tenant container platform.
scenes.headline: Isolation, but make it VM

visual.bottom_text: A VM boundary around your workload

scenes.narration: The trade off in three lines. Containers are cheap and dense. A VM boundary is a stronger wall. Pick per workload, not per religion.
scenes.headline: The trade off

scenes.narration: So the question is never containers versus VMs. It is which workloads deserve their own walls.
scenes.headline: Which workloads get walls?

scenes.narration: My take: isolate by risk, not by habit. Where do you draw the line? Tell me below.
scenes.headline: Where do you draw the line?
